facts.text: Oregon City was founded in 1829 by the Hudson's Bay Company and became the first U.S. settlement in the Oregon Country.
The city sits on the Willamette River where Willamette Falls once powered a lumber mill built by John McLoughlin in 1829.
Clackamette Park, one of Oregon City's largest parks, straddles the confluence of the Clackamas and Willamette Rivers.
The Oregon City Bridge, built in 1922, and the municipal elevator are both listed on the National Register of Historic Places.
Oregon City hosts the Museum of the Oregon Territory and the End of the Oregon Trail Interpretive Center, both featuring living‑history guides.
The city once ran an interurban trolley line to Portland until 1958, and remnants like an abandoned bridge still mark the route.
